## Toytree · Install + Theory {.smaller}

[Toytree · setup]{.eyebrow}

### A fluent tree API that returns a Toyplot canvas

```bash
pip install toytree
```

```{.python}
import toytree                    # the package itself
import toyplot                    # the rendering engine Toytree draws onto
import toyplot.svg, toyplot.png   # explicit backends for export
```

**Theory.** Toytree wraps an `ete3`-style tree object behind a single fluent
`.draw()` call. It reads **Newick / Nexus** strings or files, lets you style
**per-tip / per-node / per-edge** with simple list arguments, and ships a
collection of layouts — rectangular, circular ("c"), unrooted. Under the hood
it does **not** use matplotlib; it renders to a **Toyplot Canvas** which is
SVG-native and embeds cleanly in HTML decks like this one. For a matplotlib-
native option see `Bio.Phylo.draw` in section 12.


<!-- slide 18 -->
## Toytree · The Data {.smaller}

[Toytree · data peek]{.eyebrow}

### Hand-write a Newick string of 9 taxa

A Newick string nests sister taxa in parentheses, with `:branch_length` after
each name. Below is a small balanced clade of 9 species (`A`…`I`). We feed it to
`toytree.tree()` and peek at the parsed tree.

```{python}
#| echo: true
import toytree                                                  # tree object + .draw API

# 9-tip balanced phylogeny; numbers after ":" are branch lengths
newick = "((((A:1.2,B:1.5):2.1,(C:0.9,D:1.7):1.8):3.0," \
         "(E:2.3,F:1.6):2.7):1.5,((G:1.9,H:2.0):2.3,I:3.5):1.4);"

tre = toytree.tree(newick)                                      # parse Newick -> ToyTree
print("ntips:", tre.ntips)                                      # how many leaves
print("tips :", tre.get_tip_labels())                           # leaf names in plot order
```


<!-- slide 19 -->
## Toytree · Step 1 — Simplest Draw {.smaller}

[Toytree · build]{.eyebrow}

### 1 · `.draw()` returns (canvas, axes, mark)

The minimum call. `.draw()` returns a 3-tuple: a **Toyplot Canvas** (the SVG
container), an **axes** (the coordinate frame), and a **mark** (the tree
graphic itself). The canvas embeds straight into Quarto reveal.js as HTML/SVG
when it is the chunk's last expression — no matplotlib involved.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
```{.python code-line-numbers="1-3|5-9|11-14"}
import toytree                                          # the package

newick = "((((A:1.2,B:1.5):2.1,(C:0.9,D:1.7):1.8):3.0," \
         "(E:2.3,F:1.6):2.7):1.5,((G:1.9,H:2.0):2.3,I:3.5):1.4);"
tre = toytree.tree(newick)                              # parse Newick once

# CREATE / CALL combined — .draw() builds canvas + axes + tree mark
canvas, axes, mark = tre.draw(                          # returns 3-tuple
    width=420, height=380,                              # canvas size in px
    tip_labels_align=True,                              # right-align leaf labels
)

# Quarto auto-renders the Toyplot Canvas to inline SVG;
# fallback: toyplot.svg.render(canvas, "tre.svg") then ![](tre.svg)
canvas                                                  # last expression -> embedded
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
import toytree                                          # local import for the chunk

newick = "((((A:1.2,B:1.5):2.1,(C:0.9,D:1.7):1.8):3.0," \
         "(E:2.3,F:1.6):2.7):1.5,((G:1.9,H:2.0):2.3,I:3.5):1.4);"
tre = toytree.tree(newick)

canvas, axes, mark = tre.draw(width=420, height=380, tip_labels_align=True)
canvas
```
:::

<!-- slide 20 -->
## Toytree · Step 2 — Style Tips and Nodes {.smaller}

[Toytree · build]{.eyebrow}

### 2 · Per-tip colours, larger nodes at the root

`tip_labels_colors` takes one colour per tip (in `get_tip_labels()` order). Pass
a list straight from the Economist palette. `node_sizes` accepts a scalar or one
size per node — give the deeper nodes more weight so the eye finds the backbone.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
```{.python code-line-numbers="1-2|4-7|9-13|15-22"}
import toytree                                          # the package
from itertools import cycle                             # pad palette to ntips

newick = "((((A:1.2,B:1.5):2.1,(C:0.9,D:1.7):1.8):3.0," \
         "(E:2.3,F:1.6):2.7):1.5,((G:1.9,H:2.0):2.3,I:3.5):1.4);"
tre = toytree.tree(newick)                              # parse once

# one colour per tip from the Economist 5-hue qualitative palette
ECON_QUAL = [GREEN, BLUE, AMBER, RED, PURPLE]           # course palette
tip_colors = [c for c, _ in zip(cycle(ECON_QUAL),       # cycle palette
                                tre.get_tip_labels())]  # to length ntips

# CREATE / CALL — draw with per-tip colour + variable node sizes
canvas, axes, mark = tre.draw(
    width=460, height=400,                              # canvas size
    tip_labels_align=True,                              # cleaner leaf column
    tip_labels_colors=tip_colors,                       # one colour per tip
    node_sizes=8,                                       # base size for every node
    node_colors=INK,                                    # nodes in ink-grey
    edge_colors=MUTED,                                  # edges in muted grey
)
canvas
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}

```{python}
         "(E:2.3,F:1.6):2.7):1.5,((G:1.9,H:2.0):2.3,I:3.5):1.4);"

canvas, axes, mark = tre.draw(
    width=460, height=400,
    tip_labels_align=True,
    tip_labels_colors=tip_colors,
    node_sizes=8,
    node_colors=INK,
    edge_colors=MUTED,
)
canvas
```

<!-- slide 21 -->
## Toytree · Step 3 — Colour a Clade {.smaller}

[Toytree · build]{.eyebrow}

### 3 · Spotlight the (A,B,C,D) clade in RED

Find the **most-recent common ancestor (MRCA)** of a set of tips with
`get_mrca_node()`, list its descendants, then build per-edge colours: RED on
the clade's edges, GREY for everything else. The story-colour rule applies —
one clade in red, all else neutral.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
```{.python code-line-numbers="1|3-6|8-12|14-19|21-27"}
import toytree                                          # the package

newick = "((((A:1.2,B:1.5):2.1,(C:0.9,D:1.7):1.8):3.0," \
         "(E:2.3,F:1.6):2.7):1.5,((G:1.9,H:2.0):2.3,I:3.5):1.4);"
tre = toytree.tree(newick)                              # parse once

# pick the clade we want to spotlight by its leaf set
clade_tips = ["A", "B", "C", "D"]                       # the four sister taxa
mrca = tre.get_mrca_node(*clade_tips)                   # MRCA node object
clade_idx = {n.idx for n in mrca.get_descendants()} | {mrca.idx}  # node idxs in clade

# build edge colours — RED for clade edges, GREY for the rest
edge_colors = [RED if n.idx in clade_idx else GREY      # one colour per node (nnodes)
               for n in tre.treenode.traverse()]

# CREATE / CALL — draw with the highlighted edges
canvas, axes, mark = tre.draw(
    width=480, height=400,                              # canvas size
    tip_labels_align=True,                              # leaf column aligned
    edge_colors=edge_colors,                            # per-edge colour list
    edge_widths=2.2,                                    # thicker to read the spotlight
    node_sizes=0,                                       # nodes off; clade reads via edge
)
canvas
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
import toytree

newick = "((((A:1.2,B:1.5):2.1,(C:0.9,D:1.7):1.8):3.0," \
         "(E:2.3,F:1.6):2.7):1.5,((G:1.9,H:2.0):2.3,I:3.5):1.4);"
tre = toytree.tree(newick)

clade_tips = ["A", "B", "C", "D"]
try:
    mrca = tre.get_mrca_node(*clade_tips)
    clade_idx = {n.idx for n in mrca.get_descendants()} | {mrca.idx}
except AttributeError:
    # older toytree: fall back to mrca via tip-label idx lookup
    mrca_idx = tre.get_mrca_idx_from_tip_labels(names=clade_tips)
    mrca = tre.idx_dict[mrca_idx]
    clade_idx = {n.idx for n in mrca.get_descendants()} | {mrca.idx}

edge_colors = [RED if n.idx in clade_idx else GREY
               for n in tre.treenode.traverse()]

canvas, axes, mark = tre.draw(
    width=480, height=400,
    tip_labels_align=True,
    edge_colors=edge_colors,
    edge_widths=2.2,
    node_sizes=0,
)
canvas
```
:::
::::


<!-- slide 22 -->
## Toytree · Step 4 — Circular Layout {.smaller}

[Toytree · build]{.eyebrow}

### 4 · Same tree, radial display

Add `layout="c"` and the same data renders as a circular phylogeny — useful
when you have many tips or want to compare to a circos-style figure. The
spotlight colours port over unchanged; only the layout argument is new.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
```{.python code-line-numbers="14-19"}
import toytree                                          # the package

newick = "((((A:1.2,B:1.5):2.1,(C:0.9,D:1.7):1.8):3.0," \
         "(E:2.3,F:1.6):2.7):1.5,((G:1.9,H:2.0):2.3,I:3.5):1.4);"
tre = toytree.tree(newick)

clade_tips = ["A", "B", "C", "D"]                       # same clade
mrca = tre.get_mrca_node(*clade_tips)                   # MRCA node
clade_idx = {n.idx for n in mrca.get_descendants()} | {mrca.idx}
edge_colors = [RED if n.idx in clade_idx else GREY      # same per-edge colours
               for n in tre.treenode.traverse() if not n.is_root()]

# CREATE / CALL — only layout="c" changes
canvas, axes, mark = tre.draw(
    width=460, height=460,                              # square canvas for radial
    layout="c",                                         # "c" = circular
    edge_colors=edge_colors,                            # spotlight ports over
    edge_widths=2.0,
    tip_labels_align=True,                              # radial tip alignment
)
canvas
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}

```{python}
except AttributeError:
    mrca_idx = tre.get_mrca_idx_from_tip_labels(names=clade_tips)
    mrca = tre.idx_dict[mrca_idx]
    clade_idx = {n.idx for n in mrca.get_descendants()} | {mrca.idx}

edge_colors = [RED if n.idx in clade_idx else GREY
               for n in tre.treenode.traverse()]

canvas, axes, mark = tre.draw(
    width=460, height=460,
    layout="c",
    edge_colors=edge_colors,

    tip_labels_align=True,
)
canvas
```

<!-- slide 23 -->
## Toytree · Takeaway {.smaller}

[Toytree · recap]{.eyebrow}

### Five lines, publication-quality

::: {.takeaway}
[The recipe]{.tl}
1. **`toytree.tree(newick)`** parses every standard tree format.
2. **`.draw()`** returns a Toyplot Canvas — SVG-native, embeds straight into
   reveal.js / HTML / notebooks. No matplotlib needed.
3. **Per-tip / per-node / per-edge styling** via simple list arguments —
   `tip_labels_colors`, `node_sizes`, `edge_colors`.
4. **MRCA + descendants** is the standard pattern for clade highlights.
5. **`layout="c"`** flips rectangular to circular without changing anything else.
:::

**Compare with:** `Bio.Phylo.draw` (section 12) gives you a matplotlib-native
tree on the same `plt.subplots()` axes you use everywhere else — pick that one
when you need to stack a tree above a heatmap. Reach for **Toytree** when the
tree itself is the figure and you want pixel-perfect SVG output.
